config.title: Scroll-driven animations

intro.title: Scroll-driven animations
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple webpage where elements animate as you scroll, such as text fading in or images sliding into view. You will learn the core concept of scroll-driven animations, which link animation progress directly to the scroll position of the page. The main technology involved is CSS, using properties like `animation-timeline` and `scroll()` to create these effects. This is a beginner-friendly introduction to making websites feel more dynamic and interactive without needing JavaScript.
intro.usecase: Scroll-driven animations are a key pattern for creating engaging, modern user interfaces that respond to user interaction. You'll see them in product landing pages, where elements fade in or slide as you scroll down the page, and in long-form articles where images or diagrams animate into view as you read. As a developer, you'll implement these to build interactive dashboards with charts that reveal data on scroll, or to create immersive storytelling websites where content transitions are tied to the user's scroll position, enhancing the overall user experience.

objectives: Implement a basic scroll-driven animation using the `animation-timeline` property.
Configure an element's animation to progress based on the scroll position of its container.
Construct a keyframe animation that responds dynamically to user scrolling.
Apply the `scroll()` function to link an animation timeline directly to the scrollbar.
Manipulate animation playback by binding it to the vertical scroll axis.
Control animation direction and progress by scrolling up and down the page.
Integrate scroll-driven animations with existing CSS properties to enhance visual feedback.

steps.title: Create a basic HTML structure with scrollable content
steps.instruction: Create an HTML file with a container div and multiple content sections that will be animated as we scroll. Start by writing the basic HTML structure with a container element and at least three content sections.
steps.hint: Begin with the HTML doctype declaration, then create a container element (like a div with class 'container') and inside it add several section elements (like divs with class 'section').

steps.title: Use animation-timeline: scroll() to make animation scroll-driven
steps.instruction: In the .content-section CSS rule, add the animation-timeline property with the value scroll() to connect the slideIn animation to scroll progress.
steps.hint: Add animation-timeline: scroll(); after the existing animation property. This will make the animation progress as you scroll instead of playing automatically.

steps.title: Specify animation-range to control when animation starts and ends
steps.instruction: Add the animation-range property to the .content-section rule to define when the animation should start and end during scrolling. Use the value 'cover 0% 100%' to make the animation span the entire scrollable area of the element.
steps.hint: The animation-range property accepts values like 'cover 0% 100%' where the first percentage is the start point and the second is the end point. Place it after the animation property in your CSS rule.
